materials.analysis:
As we enter the 2023-2024 period, the inflationary environment is expected to remain volatile due to supply chain disruptions, geopolitical tensions, and the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. Historically, gold has been a popular inflation hedge due to its strong inverse correlation with inflation and its ability to retain purchasing power during periods of high inflation. 

Within the next two-year period, we anticipate gold prices to range from $1,300 to $1,800 per ounce, considering the factors mentioned above. This will provide an opportunity for investors to reallocate their portfolio, taking advantage of the price movements to generate positive absolute returns.

For the allocated 10% to Gold, we should expect a slight decline due to potential interest rate increases, which could have a mixed impact on gold prices. On the other hand, a 5% allocation to Silver is recommended as it tends to correlate with gold prices but is expected to exhibit higher price volatility. This will enable the portfolio to take advantage of the favorable price movements of both commodities.

Throughout this period, it's crucial to maintain visibility over the overall reallocation of assets. We propose rebalancing the portfolio when it drifts more than 5% from its target allocation, triggering a further evaluation of the portfolio composition and allocation to commodities.

For the materials asset class, maintain a 10% allocation to gold. Rebalance the portfolio when the drift exceeds 5% from its target allocation and re-evaluate commodity allocation.
